- Affected part: leaf sheath/stalk surface
- Numerous small dark black specks aggregated in patches
- Green background tissue
- No rust pustules, no lesion halos

Top candidates: **Physoderma brown spot** (dark purplish-black spots on midrib/sheath), **Tar spot** (black tar-like raised stromata), **Goss wilt** (freckles). Let me compare reference images.
The test image closely resembles both Physoderma brown spot (dark spots on sheath) and Tar spot (black tar-like spots). Let me check a few more references.
Goss wilt doesn't match (shows bacterial exudate + streaks). Physoderma stalk rot doesn't match (shows black node breakage). Let me view two more references for confirmation.

Neither Stewart's wilt (stunted seedlings) nor Anthracnose stalk rot (shredded pith/black rind) matches the test image.

**Final Analysis:**

The test image shows a corn leaf sheath with dense, small, dark black spots aggregated in large patches on green tissue. Comparing to references:

- **Physoderma brown spot**: The reference top-left panel shows dark spots on the stalk/sheath area that closely matches. Description: "dark purplish to black oval spots also occur on the midrib" — the sheath/midrib zone is exactly where these appear.
- **Tar spot**: Shows small circular raised black stromata on leaf blades — the spots in the test image appear on the sheath and are more aggregated/irregular than discrete circular tar spots.
- All other candidates (Goss wilt, Anthracnose stalk rot, Physoderma stalk rot, Stewart's wilt) clearly don't match.

The dense dark spotting on the leaf sheath, aggregated in patches while the surrounding tissue remains green, is most consistent with **Physoderma brown spot** (dark midrib/sheath lesions). The pattern in the Physoderma brown spot reference (top-left panel showing dark spots on sheath tissue) is the closest visual match.
